svg.aria-label: A decoder card for zero mass participation in ETABS. Three mock modal participation tables show the tell-tale patterns: a table frozen near zero in every mode, a table that is zero in the early modes with translation appearing suddenly at a high mode number, and a table showing zero lateral participation alongside an absurdly high frequency. Each pattern points down to its cause family: no mass in the model, local modes consuming the early count, or the building locked out by a restraint. Small sketches show an empty mass source, a single wall panel vibrating in isolation, and a diaphragm pinned against translation. A fourth family, too few modes, is the only one where adding modes is the right fix.
svg.text: Read the Table, Find the Cause
Three patterns in the modal participating mass ratios, and what each one means.
Pattern B: zero, then a jump
a tall building cannot be this stiff

g.text: · mass not lumped to the storey

svg.text: Read the total mass. Hand-check it
A fraction of expected? Stop here.

g.text: · a wall, deck or isolated member
· each local mode consumes a mode

svg.text: Animate modes 1 to 3. If one element
flaps instead of the building swaying,
fix connectivity, not the mode count.
Apply a static lateral load. If the
building barely deflects, it's not stiff,
Pattern D: present, climbing, but stuck under 90% → TOO FEW MODES
The mass is real and the behaviour is right. Add modes, or switch to Ritz vectors, which reach the target with fewer modes.
The only family where "add more modes" is the fix. For A, B and C it just hides the problem.
Zero participation is the model telling you, in plain numbers:
the mass isn't there · the early modes are local · the building can't move
Read the table. Animate the first three modes. Fix the cause, not the number.
